summary: Ten comment-endorsed tools, apps, books, and videos from the prior-day HN front page.

items.name: agent-shell
items.source_story_title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop for macOS and Windows
items.summary: Emacs interface for coding agents, praised for deeply customizable workflows.
items.why_included: A daily user explicitly praises the interface's hackability.
items.evidence: gnufied uses agent-shell as their sole agent interface and praises workflow customization.

evidence_sources.author: gnufied
evidence_sources.excerpt: What makes this great is infinite hack-ability of the interface

items.name: JUCE
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Audionaut – an open-source cross-platform multitrack audio editor
items.summary: Cross-platform C++ audio framework; a longtime user praises reliability and community support.
items.why_included: Decades of first-hand use provide a concrete reliability endorsement.
items.evidence: vltmrkls praises decades of reliability and a maintained forum; r2ob flags commercial licensing barriers.

evidence_sources.author: vltmrkls
evidence_sources.excerpt: i have been using JUCE for decades and it's been very reliable and stable with a well maintained forum.

evidence_sources.author: r2ob
evidence_sources.excerpt: JUCE is open source, but it has a lot of barriers for commercial products.

items.name: Pyxel
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Pyxel – A Python retro game engine with built-in art and sound editors
items.summary: Python retro-game engine with art and sound editors; praised for quick, playful coding.
items.why_included: An independent user endorses the engine after making a retro demo.
items.evidence: gregkb enjoyed recreating demoscene effects and found setup and initial coding easy.

evidence_sources.author: gregkb
evidence_sources.excerpt: had such a great time with Pyxel! was great fun to recreate some of the demo scene effects from my childhood.

items.name: Mozilla VPN
items.source_story_title: Court agrees with EFF: Utah's VPN law demands a technical impossibility
items.summary: Personal VPN with ad-blocking DNS; a user likes it despite occasional website blocks.
items.why_included: A first-hand privacy endorsement includes a practical access caveat.
items.evidence: not_a_bot_4sho likes Mozilla VPN's privacy and DNS blocking but sometimes encounters blocked sites while using a VPN.

evidence_sources.author: not_a_bot_4sho
evidence_sources.excerpt: I like Mozilla VPN for personal privacy. (Note: it has ad blocking DNS built in which is nice!) I occasionally get blocked by websites or services, especially streaming apps, if I'm on VPN.

items.name: Pass2U Wallet
items.summary: App for putting cards into Apple Wallet; described as clunky but effective.
items.why_included: A user explicitly endorses the app for replacing barcode-only apps with wallet passes.
items.evidence: neom uses Pass2U Wallet and says it works well despite a clunky interface.

evidence_sources.author: neom
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use an app called pass2 u wallet for this, it's clunky but works well. No affiliation.

items.name: Pass4Wallet
items.summary: Free iPhone app for creating Apple Wallet passes from store cards and coupons.
items.why_included: A fresh first-hand recommendation resurfaces this useful app after its 90-day cooldown.
items.evidence: Lalabadie describes Pass4Wallet as their recent go-to among free options.

evidence_sources.author: Lalabadie
evidence_sources.excerpt: Pass4Wallet has been my go-to recently (among the free options)
